# Android settings portability implementation

Status: source implemented, **UNVERIFIED**. No compilation, unit tests, instrumented tests, APK or device checks run. Parent owns verification. No commits, pushes, Boat, SDK, VM or build jobs started. `git diff --check` passed for owned paths.

## Implemented

- `app/.../settings/ProcessStores.kt` owns one lazy SharedPreferences, DataStore and Room instance. Hilt providers use its public getters. Public access defaults to denied and only opens after startup plus component healing succeed. The importer has private adapter access; recovery Retry never opens the public gate.
- `FarhanApplication.onCreate` joins a settings worker before `super.onCreate`, Hilt, ACRA and WorkManager. An absent journal touches no settings stores. Blocking or unexpected recovery failures skip normal initialization. Startup checks `StartupResult.allowsNormalOperation`, including conservative JOURNAL_WRITE_FAILED handling.
- `AndroidSettingsStores.kt` uses SharedPreferences `getAll` and one synchronous commit, DataStore public typed read/edit on IO with the same process instance, and Room's writable database with `SqlConfigurationRowsStore` through one SQL transaction. No history table statements were added. Confirmed stage opens/migrates the Room schema first.
- `PrivateSettingsFiles.kt` stores the import journal under `no_backup/settings_import_v1` using AtomicFile, explicit FD sync before finishWrite, an 8 MiB byte bound, strict UTF-8, duplicate/member/type/version checks and sealed phase-specific members. Nested core codec strings preserve raw previous keys/types plus preview/source and terminal failure details. Only absent files return null; corrupt records throw JournalUnreadableException. This private file can contain destination credentials and never goes to SAF or logs.
- `RecoveryComponents.kt` enables the plain RecoveryActivity marker, snapshots raw overrides atomically before disabling all other listed activities, services, receivers and providers with GET_DISABLED_COMPONENTS, and requests kill only if normal components changed. Repeated blocked startup has no component writes once all are off. Healing restores exact raw states, removes snapshot after restoration and disables recovery last. A normal launch with marker disabled performs no PackageManager writes.
- `RecoveryActivity` is a disabled-by-default launcher entry without Hilt. It provides Retry, failure reason/component codes and Close. Successful Retry heals components while keeping the store gate closed, then requires close/process kill/reopen. UI warns about home selection and notification/accessibility grants.
- `SettingsBackupActivity` is a permanent entry from MainActivity. Export validates and encodes on a worker before CreateDocument launches. Unknown names are shown before choosing a file. OpenDocument reads at most 1 MiB plus one byte; the full preview uses a memory journal through the actual coordinator. Cancellation creates no real Staged record. Only explicit Replace and close opens Room and writes the durable real stage, then closes/kills. Terminal outcomes require acknowledgment before a new import. SAF file IO runs on workers. No storage permission was added.
- New shared Android library `:settings_android` exposes `ly.com.tahaben.settings_android.AndroidSettingsValidator` for both app and rescue. It depends on the core catalog, existing ScheduleCodec, real notification/domain enums, and existing theme enums. Embedded JSON is parsed strictly before the existing decoder. Legacy 23:59 and short-window migration calls DaySchedule.repairLegacy; original schedule text is preserved. No new schedule algorithm or quiet defaults were introduced.
- Focused unrun instrumented tests cover raw previous type/exact-long preservation, duplicate/truncated journal refusal, terminal failure retention/clear, legacy schedule endpoint acceptance, bad embedded JSON, and real theme names including onboarding's Unknown sentinel.

## Limits and required verification

Widget profile source integration is now implemented, still UNVERIFIED. `WidgetProfiles` in settings_android defines five typed user fields using real ThemeColors/UIModeAppearance and HORIZONTAL/VERTICAL wire styles. StrictPreferenceJson is reused for profile decoding. Canonical JSON arrays live only in main DataStore key imported_widget_profiles_v1, now registered as one catalog STRING entry. Legacy maps with only derived state produce no profile; partial maps use the existing Classic/FOLLOW_SYSTEM/VERTICAL/false/32 defaults. Profiles are validated, deduplicated and sorted. Text size allows 8..48, including odd legacy sizes; the current UI offers 8..48 in steps of two.

ProcessStores.export reads installed Glance IDs and states via public APIs, extracts only the five user keys and merges with unused imported profiles. A read-only preferences snapshot supplies the merged string to the actual SettingsExporter; export does not mutate stores. Invalid profiles fail export. The normal atomic DataStore import restores the imported choices. WidgetConfigActivity preserves its own configured user choices; when none exist it previews the first imported style. All saved choices are offered as explicit buttons. Widget OS IDs, usage/loading state and nonpersisted WorkManager refresh interval are excluded. Preview explains adding widgets again and choosing saved styles. Six focused shared-library tests plus one app renderer-enum parity test were added, all unrun.

Shared helper APIs in ly.com.tahaben.settings_android: WidgetProfiles.KEY, USER_KEYS; fromLegacy(List<Map<String,SettingValue>>):List<WidgetProfile>; merge(vararg List<WidgetProfile>):List<WidgetProfile>; encode(List<WidgetProfile>):String; decode(String):List<WidgetProfile>; validate(WidgetProfile):Unit. WidgetProfile fields: themeColors:ThemeColors, uiModeAppearance:UIModeAppearance, style:WidgetStyle, compareWithYesterday:Boolean, textSize:Int.

Raw NaN/Infinity cannot be represented by the core JSON codec. Such a destination snapshot fails its Applying journal write before any mutation and conservatively blocks until recovery can be resolved. DataStore byte-array values are not in SettingValue; no current app uses were found during inventory. If encountered, the Android adapter raises UNSUPPORTED_STORAGE_TYPE without a value. Normal export reports that fixed code; a startup snapshot failure remains PREVIOUS_UNREADABLE. SharedPreferences supports no double value and rejects any impossible requested double.

Required parent checks: compile app plus shared library and all new Android tests; merged-manifest provider/initializer audit; real export/import round trip; journal/component crash points and component snapshot/toggle failure; HOME selection, listener/accessibility grants and WorkManager scheduling after recovery; startup timing with a realistic 1 MiB document. The component protocol is implemented directly against PackageManager and has no fake crash-sweep test yet. AtomicFile durability still needs device fault-injection evidence. No physical recovery or signing-key transition has been attempted. Widget completeness requires a real installed-widget plus imported-unused-profile round trip and config-screen checks.

## Handoff check-in

Only production widget text-size write found is WidgetConfigActivity's save path. It receives the 8..48 dropdown choices, the default 32, an existing own value or a validated imported profile. No separate production write outside that range was found. Odd 8..48 values remain accepted for legacy compatibility.

The normal channel-priority UI derives offsets from the difference of priorities 1..4, but the persisted setter and domain interface accept any Int. The validator's inferred -3..3 bound was therefore removed. Catalog Int32 validation is retained without an invented semantic bound.

Export snapshots main DataStore before reading Glance states. Any widget enumeration/read/type/profile failure propagates and aborts the entire export before document creation. No profile is silently omitted because of an error. Export adds the merged profile key only to a read-only in-memory PreferencesStore snapshot; it makes no DataStore write and uses the same single process DataStore instance as Hilt/import.

## Parent lifecycle fix

Prepared exports now live in a bounded atomic private record under no_backup until the document picker returns. Recreation while the picker is open can reload and validate the document instead of silently losing an Activity field. Cancel discards the pending record; a successful write clears it. Document operations use one worker queue per Activity, so an arriving picker result is not dropped while the startup outcome check runs. The worker shuts down on destroy. Android compilation and recreation/process-death exercises remain unrun.
# Settings rescue helper: green report

**Status: source and tests written, nothing compiled or run.** No builds, jobs, Boat, VM, emulator, commits or child agents were started by this author. Over the 30 minute flag (about 40 minutes of wall time). Parent owns compile, tests, merged-manifest audit and device checks.

Module: `settings_rescue/` (applicationId `ly.com.tahaben.farhan_rescue`, minSdk 30, compile/target from the catalog). Only `settings_rescue/**` and this file were written. Canonical core, app and `settings_android` were read only.

## Parent patch instructions

`settings.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
// inside dependencyResolutionManagement.repositories
maven("https://jitpack.io") {
    content { includeGroupByRegex("com\\.github\\.MuntashirAkon.*") }   // libadb-android + spake2-android
}
// below the other includes
include(":settings_rescue")
```

Nothing else in root files. Versions are literals in `settings_rescue/build.gradle.kts` (no catalog edit). `settings_rescue` depends on `:settings_portability`, `:settings_android`, `:core` (needed on the compile classpath for `ThemeColors`; `settings_android` declares it `implementation`). No Hilt, Compose or main-app modules.

## Dependency and API facts (primary sources, checked 2026-11-17/18)

1. libadb-android 3.1.1 `AbsAdbConnectionManager` (tagged source): `protected abstract PrivateKey getPrivateKey()`, `Certificate getCertificate()`, `String getDeviceName()`; public `setApi(int)`, `setHostAddress(String)`, `setTimeout(long, TimeUnit)`, `setThrowOnUnauthorised(boolean)`, `boolean pair(String host, int port, String code) throws Exception`, `boolean connect(String host, int port) throws IOException, InterruptedException, AdbPairingRequiredException`, `AdbStream openStream(String)`, `disconnect()`, `close()` (close also destroys the key, so the helper calls `disconnect()`). `AdbPairingRequiredException` and `AdbAuthenticationFailedException` extend `Exception`, package `io.github.muntashirakon.adb`.
2. `AdbInputStream.read()` returns a signed byte; the helper uses only `read(byte[], int, int)`.
3. When the daemon closes a stream while a reader waits with nothing queued, `AdbStream.read` throws `IOException("Stream closed.")` instead of -1. The helper treats that message as end of stream, which means a dropped connection looks like a normal end. Completeness therefore never comes from the stream; every copy is checked against `stat` length and `sha256sum`.
4. JitPack `libadb-android:3.1.1` pom lists `annotation:1.9.1`, `bcprov-jdk15to18:1.81`, `spake2-android:2.2.1` at **runtime** scope. spake2-android is on JitPack too and is **LGPL-3.0**. libadb is dual GPL-3.0-or-later / Apache-2.0; notices in `NOTICE.md` and `res/raw/third_party_notices.txt` (shown by the Licenses button).
5. `org.conscrypt:conscrypt-android:2.5.3` (aar, Apache-2.0) and `org.bouncycastle:bcpkix-jdk15to18:1.81` exist on Maven Central. libadb's `SslUtils` loads `org.conscrypt.OpenSSLProvider` by name and `PairingConnectionCtx` calls `org.conscrypt.Conscrypt.exportKeyingMaterial` when present: no hidden-API exemption anywhere. The certificate comes from `JcaX509v3CertificateBuilder` (public API), RSA-2048 software key, SHA512withRSA, valid one day.
6. `exec:` has no exit status and merges stderr into the stream (adbd shell service without shell_v2). So: every command whose success matters ends `&& echo farhan-rescue-ok` and success is that sentinel on the last line (never empty output); binary copies and sentinel commands send stderr to `/dev/null`; only the uid probe keeps stderr, to classify `run-as` errors.
7. `run-as` (AOSP `run-as.cpp`, main): usage `run-as <package> [--user <uid>] <command>`; errors `unknown package`, `package not debuggable`, `package not an application`, `user id too big`, `only 'shell' or 'root' users can run this program`. It `chdir`s into the data directory, so file arguments are relative. Unknown text fails closed (`RUN_AS_UNRECOGNIZED`).
8. `farhan_db` is the combined Room database (`FarhanDatabase`; `apps_db` and `TimeLimitEntity` live there, `DatabaseCombineHelper` merges the legacy `notifications_db`/`usage_db`). A pre-merge install that never ran the merge would keep launcher rows in another file; the helper reads only `farhan_db` (see limitations).

## Answers to the check-in questions

1. **Absent vs failed.** Listings run through `ls -1 DIR 2>/dev/null && echo SENTINEL`. The data-directory root (`ls -1 .`) and `files` are listed first and must succeed. A directory is "absent" only when its parent's successful listing lacks it. A directory that is listed but whose own `ls` has no sentinel is `LISTING_FAILED`. Every planned file is then `stat`ed; no sentinel is `STAT_FAILED`. Empty plan is `NOTHING_TO_EXPORT`. Tests: `CaptureEngineTest.failedListingIsAnErrorButAnAbsentDirectoryIsFine`, `emptyDataDirectoryIsRefused`.
2. **UID belongs to the requested user.** `AdbOutput.uidMatchesUser(uid, user)` is `uid / 100000 == user && uid % 100000 in 10000..19999` (Android `UserHandle` arithmetic, Long math). A mismatch is `UID_USER_MISMATCH` before force-stop. Tests: `AdbCommandTest.uidMustBelongToTheRequestedUser`, `CaptureEngineTest.uidOfAnotherUserIsRefusedBeforeAnyStop`.
3. **Bounds.** Caps: prefs 8 MiB, main DataStore 8 MiB, widget file 64 KiB (at most 256, 4 MiB together), DB 128 MiB, WAL 32 MiB, journal 32 MiB, whole capture 192 MiB. All come from `stat` and are enforced before the first copy; each copy stops at its own stat size (a larger stream throws and becomes `SOURCE_CHANGED`). Text outputs: listing 64 KiB, stat/hash 4 KiB, uid probe 4 KiB, version dump 8 MiB streamed with early stop, and one shared 16 MiB output budget per job. Tests: `sizeBoundsAreEnforcedBeforeAnyCopy`.
4. **Ambiguity in capture/cancel.** (a) After a kill the service may still be writing for a few milliseconds; the UI deletes the job directory immediately and again at the next start, so a last write can only land in a directory that the next sweep removes. (b) A bridge that dies between the pairing and connect steps leaves the identity file; it is erased by cancel, reset, completed capture, failed export, timeout, 30 minute expiry, or Activity destroy when something was running or the screen is finishing. (c) With no `sha256sum` on the phone the capture still succeeds with integrity `SIZE_ONLY`; this is reported in `CaptureFacts` but the review screen does not show it yet (see open items).
5. **Stale replies (parent finding).** Each bind creates a new generation and a new reply `Messenger` closed over it. Every request carries an operation id (`op`) that the bridge echoes on every event. `EventRouting.accept` drops an event unless generation matches, the id equals the inflight operation, and the event kind fits that operation (a `Captured` only finishes an export, a `Paired` only a pair). Test: `BridgeSupervisionTest.staleOrMismatchedEventsAreIgnored`.
6. **Binder liveness (parent finding).** `BridgeSession.killIfLive` also requires `pingBinder()` true at the kill site and a Hello from the current generation; the UI also sends `CANCEL` so the service ends itself first. Test: `killIsOnlyAllowedWhileBoundHelloedAndBinderAlive`.
7. **Small fixes applied:** `pair()` returning `false` is `PAIR_FAILED`; `PRAGMA quick_check` must return exactly one row `ok`; a failed export erases the identity and the raw job.

## What is in the module

Pure JVM (no Android imports; snapshot candidates for a SDK-free run) under `settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/`:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `input/RescueInput.kt` | `PackageName`, `AndroidUserId`, `TcpPort`, `PairingCode` (redacted), `LoopbackHost`, `JobId`, `SourceTarget` |
| `adb/AdbCommand.kt` | sealed `AdbCommand` (only service strings the helper can open), `AdbOutput` parsers |
| `adb/RemoteFiles.kt` | allowlist, `CapturePlanner`, size roles |
| `adb/RemoteShell.kt` | the only door to the device |
| `capture/CaptureEngine.kt` | full device sequence, `FailureCode`, facts |

## Answers to the check-in questions

1. **Absent vs failed.** Listings run through `ls -1 DIR 2>/dev/null && echo SENTINEL`. The data-directory root (`ls -1 .`) and `files` are listed first and must succeed. A directory is "absent" only when its parent's successful listing lacks it. A directory that is listed but whose own `ls` has no sentinel is `LISTING_FAILED`. Every planned file is then `stat`ed; no sentinel is `STAT_FAILED`. Empty plan is `NOTHING_TO_EXPORT`. Tests: `CaptureEngineTest.failedListingIsAnErrorButAnAbsentDirectoryIsFine`, `emptyDataDirectoryIsRefused`.
2. **UID belongs to the requested user.** `AdbOutput.uidMatchesUser(uid, user)` is `uid / 100000 == user && uid % 100000 in 10000..19999` (Android `UserHandle` arithmetic, Long math). A mismatch is `UID_USER_MISMATCH` before force-stop. Tests: `AdbCommandTest.uidMustBelongToTheRequestedUser`, `CaptureEngineTest.uidOfAnotherUserIsRefusedBeforeAnyStop`.
3. **Bounds.** Caps: prefs 8 MiB, main DataStore 8 MiB, widget file 64 KiB (at most 256, 4 MiB together), DB 128 MiB, WAL 32 MiB, journal 32 MiB, whole capture 192 MiB. All come from `stat` and are enforced before the first copy; each copy stops at its own stat size (a larger stream throws and becomes `SOURCE_CHANGED`). Text outputs: listing 64 KiB, stat/hash 4 KiB, uid probe 4 KiB, version dump 8 MiB streamed with early stop, and one shared 16 MiB output budget per job. Tests: `sizeBoundsAreEnforcedBeforeAnyCopy`.
4. **Ambiguity in capture/cancel.** (a) After a kill the service may still be writing for a few milliseconds; the UI deletes the job directory immediately and again at the next start, so a last write can only land in a directory that the next sweep removes. (b) A bridge that dies between the pairing and connect steps leaves the identity file; it is erased by cancel, reset, completed capture, failed export, timeout, 30 minute expiry, or Activity destroy when something was running or the screen is finishing. (c) With no `sha256sum` on the phone the capture still succeeds with integrity `SIZE_ONLY`; this is reported in `CaptureFacts` but the review screen does not show it yet (see open items).
5. **Stale replies (parent finding).** Each bind creates a new generation and a new reply `Messenger` closed over it. Every request carries an operation id (`op`) that the bridge echoes on every event. `EventRouting.accept` drops an event unless generation matches, the id equals the inflight operation, and the event kind fits that operation (a `Captured` only finishes an export, a `Paired` only a pair). Test: `BridgeSupervisionTest.staleOrMismatchedEventsAreIgnored`.
6. **Binder liveness (parent finding).** `BridgeSession.killIfLive` also requires `pingBinder()` true at the kill site and a Hello from the current generation; the UI also sends `CANCEL` so the service ends itself first. Test: `killIsOnlyAllowedWhileBoundHelloedAndBinderAlive`.
7. **Small fixes applied:** `pair()` returning `false` is `PAIR_FAILED`; `PRAGMA quick_check` must return exactly one row `ok`; a failed export erases the identity and the raw job.

I'm reviewing the `run-as` usage and checking it against AOSP's syntax, which looks correct. I'm also questioning whether the `exec:` service runs the command through a shell, since that affects how the command is parsed.

I'm checking how adbd runs the `exec:` command, and it goes through `sh -c`, so the shell operators like `&&` and `2>/dev/null` are interpreted outside run-as. The sentinel then only reflects run-as's exit status. I'm also confirming that the single-quoted `stat` format string reaches stat as one argument, and that toybox's `%F` output "regular empty file" is still caught by the "regular" prefix check.

I'm going over how Android's SharedPreferences handles the `.bak` file: a leftover backup means a write was interrupted, so on load it gets restored over the main file and the backup is the consistent copy to read from. Since the app was force-stopped, that still holds. I'm also noting that pending `apply()` writes may be lost on kill, though whatever was flushed before that is kept, and DataStore's temp-then-rename write should leave nothing half-written.

I'm checking how the WAL copy behaves: Room's default WAL mode means the `-wal` file has to sit beside the copied database under the same name, and without the `-shm` file SQLite rebuilds its index from the WAL on open, validating frames by checksum. I'm also turning to the DataStore files used by the widgets.

I'm checking where Glance keeps each widget's state: the file key comes from the app widget ID, so the DataStore file should be `files/datastore/appWidget-12.preferences_pb`.

I'm checking whether the Farhan widget relies on Glance's PreferencesGlanceStateDefinition or a custom state definition, and then I'll move on to reading the capture engine.

 26 │ /**
 27 │  * Stages, applies and recovers a full settings replace across the three stores.
 28 │  *
 29 │  * Usage: [stage] while the app runs; [startup] first thing in the next process, before Hilt-created stores,
 30 │  * WorkManager or any screen reads settings.
 31 │  *
 32 │  * Invariants:
 33 │  *  - CLAIM(stage-no-write): stage never changes a store; an invalid file changes nothing, and the only durable
 34 │  *    write is the Staged journal record, after every check passed.
 35 │  *  - CLAIM(domain-replace): apply removes catalog Configuration keys absent from the desired set and leaves every
 36 │  *    other key (internal flags, usage counters, unknown keys) untouched. Destination automation is an import-reset
 37 │  *    domain, separate from transferable configuration: the same preferences commit removes its credential and
 38 │  *    receipts and writes enabled=false. Previous captures these raw values too, so rollback restores them exactly.
 39 │  *  - CLAIM(journal-first): the Applying record, which holds previous and desired, is durable before the first

 45 │  *    the desired configuration or every component holds the previous one.

 67 │         val existing = try {
 68 │             journal.read()
 69 │         } catch (unreadable: Exception) {
 70 │             return StageResult.NotStaged(NotStagedReason.JOURNAL_UNAVAILABLE)
 71 │         }
 72 │         if (existing != null && existing !is ImportJournal.Staged) return StageResult.NotStaged(NotStagedReason.IMPORT_IN_PROGRESS)
 73 │ 
 74 │         val settings = when (val decoded = PortableSettingsCodec.decode(fileBytes, limits)) {
 75 │             is DecodeResult.Valid -> decoded.settings
 76 │             is DecodeResult.Invalid -> return StageResult.Rejected(decoded.error)
 77 │         }

 79 │         ConfigurationChecks.semanticProblem(validator, settings.configuration)?.let { return StageResult.Rejected(it) }
 80 │ 
 81 │         val preview = ImportPreview(
 82 │             source = settings.source,
 83 │             sharedPreferenceCount = settings.configuration.sharedPreferences.size,

107 │             is ImportJournal.RolledBack -> StartupResult.RolledBack(current.failure)

109 │             is ImportJournal.Applying -> rollBack(current.previous, ImportFailure(FailureReason.INTERRUPTED), alreadyRollingBack = false)

116 │         when (journal.read()) {
117 │             is ImportJournal.Applying, is ImportJournal.RollingBack -> true
118 │             is ImportJournal.Staged, is ImportJournal.Applied, is ImportJournal.RolledBack, null -> false
119 │         }

126 │      * unreadable journal. A failed clear propagates and leaves the terminal journal, so acknowledging can be retried.

142 │     private fun applyStaged(staged: ImportJournal.Staged): StartupResult {
143 │         val previous = try {
144 │             SettingsConfiguration(
145 │                 sharedPreferences = domainOf(SettingsStoreId.SHARED_PREFERENCES, sharedPreferences.readAll()),
146 │                 dataStore = domainOf(SettingsStoreId.DATA_STORE, dataStore.readAll()),

153 │         }

content.thinking:
I've confirmed the primary keys match the database. The journal decode path uses the codec's default depth limit of 8, which looks fine. Strings with lone surrogates could make encoding throw and block writes, which is an edge case worth keeping in mind. Next I'm checking how the exporter's outgoing classification refuses on type mismatch for a configuration.

I'm checking the exporter's outgoing classification, which refuses a configuration key with the wrong type, and an old build storing such a key would make the whole rescue fail. Next I'm comparing the settings keys used in the base app against the catalog, since any key missing from it would be listed by name but have its value dropped.

package ly.com.tahaben.settings_portability

/**
 * Checks meaning the pure module cannot know: schedule JSON, enum names and similar. The Android side
 * implements it with the existing ScheduleCodec and domain enums. Returns the first problem, or null.
 */
fun interface SemanticValidator {
    fun firstProblem(configuration: SettingsConfiguration): SemanticProblem?
}

/** Names the setting only. Never carries its value. */
data class SemanticProblem(val store: SettingsStoreId, val key: String)

/** What the rescue helper reads out of the copied source: raw files plus the already-decoded typed stores. */
data class LegacySourceSnapshot(
    val source: PortableSource,
    /** Raw `shared_prefs/shared_pref.xml`. */

I'm noticing a real risk here: if the validator rejects a value the old app stored, such as schedule JSON it tolerated by falling back to a default, the export fails outright with SETTINGS_REJECTED and the owner gets no backup at all. I need to check whether that failure is intended, since the spec rules out silent defaults for a bad schedule, which suggests rejecting is the right call.

I'm checking the widget profile path next: rescue builds `encodedProfiles` from the legacy states plus the imported ones. Glance clears a widget's state when the widget is deleted, so stale state files shouldn't leak in, and the imported profiles key is present on a fresh signed install. Then I'll look at the rescue UI and bridge for the invariants about failed captures and stale replies, starting with the bridge.

 33 │  * the same pid as a backup.

 60 │ class OperationTracker(

 76 │     fun begin(kind: OperationKind): Inflight? {

 80 │         deadlineMillis = nowMillis() + absoluteTimeoutMillis

 86 │     fun progress(id: Long) {

102 │         timer?.cancel(); timer = null
103 │         inflight = null
104 │         session.killIfLive()

106 │     }

110 │         val remaining = deadlineMillis - nowMillis()

112 │     }

# Settings portability: review round 1

Reviewer: Opus 5.5, review only. Diff `git diff c36faf1 3f5eb31 -- app settings.gradle.kts gradle settings_portability settings_android settings_rescue`. Nothing was built or run. No edits outside this file. Over the 30-minute flag (about 45 minutes).

Read in full: ImportCoordinator, ImportJournal, SettingsStores, SettingsCatalog, ConfigurationChecks, LegacyXml, LegacySettingsConverter, codec header and writer; app ProcessStores, SettingsStartup, RecoveryComponents, RecoveryActivity, AndroidSettingsStores, PrivateSettingsFiles, SettingsBackupActivity, the AppModule, MainActivity, manifest and widget diffs; settings_android validator and widget profiles; rescue AdbCommand, RemoteFiles, RemoteShell, AdbShell, CaptureEngine, RescueAdbManager, AdbBridgeService, BridgeSupervision, PrivateFiles, CopiedStores, RescueConverter, RescueConversion, RescueActivity, manifest, build file, strings. Catalog checked against every preference key constant in c36faf1: no missing setting found.

What holds up: journal-first apply, rollback across all three stores, RecoveryRequired never reported as success, reset keys refused on input and removed in the same SharedPreferences commit, raw previous values kept, the strict XML reader, sentinel-based absent-versus-failed listings, stat-before/stat-after plus digest checks, the generation/operation/kind event filter, the binder-liveness kill guard, and the SAF read-back in the helper. A SharedPreferences commit that fails after updating memory still converges, because rollback rewrites the whole file from the restored map.

SCORE[durability]: 6/10 (S1 bricks a healthy app after an update while blocked; S2 leaves the blocked-startup protocol with no executed test; S3 may keep the top-priority rescue from ever completing. Fixing all three raises it to 8-9; bar 9)
SCORE[error-paths]: 6/10 (S3's SOURCE_CHANGED advice cannot be followed; recovery text is wrong after a self-healed launch (nit). Text fixes raise it to 8; bar 6)
SCORE[security]: 8/10 (no in-model exposure: secrets never reach portable files, the journal stays in no_backup, the helper allowlist builds every shell argument from typed input; remaining items are hardening; bar 6)
SCORE[architecture]: 6/10 (S4: the full Gradle build most likely fails while configuring :settings_portability; the shared catalog, converter and validator are the right shape; bar 6)
SCORE[legibility]: 7/10 (claims are cited and sourced; the intro's "Farhan is not changed" is false (S3); bar 6)
VERDICT: CHANGES

S1 [should] [needed for bar: yes] [class: migration-safety] [concern: durability] app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/RecoveryComponents.kt:50, app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/SettingsStartup.kt:16, app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/SettingsStartup.kt:24 `heal()` replays every snapshot entry. If a recorded component no longer exists, the replay calls `setComponentEnabledSetting`, which throws `IllegalArgumentException("Component class … does not exist")`. `SettingsStartup` catches the throw and calls `block()`, so a start with consistent stores (NoImport, Applied or RolledBack) disables everything and skips Hilt. Every later start, and every Retry, throws at the same entry. Reproduction: an import blocks (rollback failed, for example storage full), so the snapshot records all components, including WorkManager's explicit ENABLED proxies. The owner installs a fixed build (the normal pilot loop) that removes or renames one receiver or service, or bumps WorkManager. Every launch now heals, throws, blocks and shows "The recovery state could not be restored". Only clear data, which deletes every setting, or a debuggable `run-as rm` gets out. Fix: in `heal()`, list the current components (the same `getPackageInfo(... GET_DISABLED_COMPONENTS)` that `block()` uses) and skip snapshot entries that are no longer there. A removed component has no state to restore. Pin it with a test from S2.

S2 [should] [needed for bar: yes] [class: test-weakness] [concern: durability] app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/RecoveryComponents.kt:17, app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/ProcessStores.kt:38, app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/SettingsStartup.kt:9 The accepted spec (spec-reply "Tests for green") requires pure JVM tests for the ProcessStores gate (after a blocking result each getter throws and no store opens; no journal opens no store) and for the component protocol over a fake PackageManager: snapshot before the first disable, kill only on change, an upgrade adding a component, exact raw-state healing, a crash after each write, and zero writes on a healthy start. None exist, and the android green report says so. The production journal (`AndroidImportJournal`, which round-trips `previous` through the codec) is covered only by an instrumented test that has not run. The 45 core tests use an in-memory journal. Reproduction by mutation: move `snapshot.write(states)` after the disable loop, call `allowNormalOperation()` before `heal()`, or drop `snapshot.clear()`. All 101 executed tests stay green. S1 is exactly the kind of bug a fake-PackageManager test catches. Fix: put the logic behind a three-method `ComponentStates` port (list, get, set) and a snapshot port, move `block`/`heal` into code the JVM can run, and add the spec's cases plus S1's. Add one ProcessStores gate test with counting store factories. Run the instrumented journal test before round 2.

S3 [should] [needed for bar: yes] [class: misleading-docs] [concern: durability] settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/capture/CaptureEngine.kt:109, settings_rescue/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:4, settings_rescue/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:28, settings_rescue/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:93 The capture assumes `am force-stop` keeps the source quiet. On a phone where old Farhan holds notification access (its main feature), NotificationManagerService handles `ACTION_PACKAGE_RESTARTED` through `ManagedServices.onPackagesChanged`, which calls `rebindServices`. Binding the listener also clears the stopped state, so the old Farhan process comes back within seconds. Each arriving notification then writes `farhan_db-wal` and `shared_pref.xml`, the after-stat differs, and the export fails with SOURCE_CHANGED. Its advice, "Make sure it is closed, then try again", cannot be followed. Force-stop also has a second effect. On Android 11-13, `AccessibilityManagerService.onHandleForceStop` removes the package's services from `ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES`, which turns off Farhan's scroll-blocker and grayscale services. The intro's "Farhan is not changed" is therefore false. The stat check fails closed, so no wrong backup is produced. The risk is that the priority-one backup never completes. Reproduction: the owner taps Stop Farhan and export while messages arrive. Copying a multi-megabyte `farhan_db` over loopback spans seconds, so SOURCE_CHANGED keeps repeating. content.text:
**VERDICT: CHANGES.** The review is in `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/research/settings-portability-review-round1.md`. It took about 45 minutes, over the 30-minute flag. I made no edits outside that file and built or ran nothing.

| Concern | Score | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| durability | 6 | 9 |
| error-paths | 6 | 6 |
| security | 8 | 6 |
| architecture | 6 | 6 |
| legibility | 7 | 6 |

All four findings are should, needed for bar:

- **S1, migration-safety** (`RecoveryComponents.kt:50`, `SettingsStartup.kt:16,24`): this can lock a healthy app out for good.
  - `heal()` replays every component in the saved snapshot. If a recorded component no longer exists after an app update, `setComponentEnabledSetting` throws.
  - `SettingsStartup` catches that and calls `block()`, so every start and every Retry ends blocked, even with consistent stores. Only clearing data, which deletes every setting, or a debuggable `run-as` gets out.
  - Realistic path: an import blocks, then the owner installs a fixed build that drops a receiver or bumps WorkManager.
  - Fix: skip snapshot entries that the current package no longer lists.
- **S2, test-weakness**: the spec required JVM tests for two things, and none exist.
  - Required: the `ProcessStores` gate, and the component block/heal protocol over a fake PackageManager.
  - The Android journal is covered only by an instrumented test that hasn't run.
  - Mutations such as writing the snapshot after the disables, or opening the gate before healing, keep all 101 tests green.
  - Fix: put the protocol behind a small port and add the spec's cases plus S1's.
- **S3, misleading-docs** (`CaptureEngine.kt:109`, `strings.xml:4,28,93`): force-stop probably doesn't keep the old app quiet. This needs a device check.
  - The system likely rebinds Farhan's notification listener right after force-stop. Each arriving notification then changes the source files, so export fails with SOURCE_CHANGED, and its advice ("make sure it is closed") can't be followed.
  - On Android 11–13, force-stop also turns off Farhan's accessibility services, so the intro's "Farhan is not changed" is false.
  - The check fails safe, so no bad backup comes out. The risk is that the priority-one rescue never completes.
  - Fix, text only: tell the owner to turn off notification access before exporting, and say that accessibility services get switched off.
- **S4, prod-wiring** (`settings_portability/build.gradle.kts:7`): the full build most likely fails while configuring `:settings_portability`.
  - The module requests the Kotlin JVM plugin with a version. The root build already loads the same Kotlin plugin through `jetbrainsKotlinAndroid apply false`, and Gradle refuses that combination.
  - Your 101-test run used the module's standalone `settings.gradle.kts`, which hides this. `./gradlew help` confirms it in seconds.
  - Fix: add `alias(libs.plugins.jetbrainsKotlinJvm) apply false` to the root `plugins {}` block.

The file also lists five nits and five hardening items. The most notable hardening item is that ACRA's sender runs in a separate `:acra` process, so startup can run there too. A crash during an unfinished import could then race two processes on the journal.

I checked the settings catalog against every preference key in c36faf1 and found nothing missing. Nothing here claims device behaviour was verified. No comment fixups.
